blocks.b: SpaceX is scheduled to launch the Starlink Group 10-19 communications mission on August 10, 2026. This dedicated flight will deploy the next batch of operational satellites to expand the global internet constellation.

The mission utilizes the workhorse Falcon 9 Block 5, the flight-proven medium-lift launch vehicle of SpaceX. This rocket is designed for high reliability and rapid turnaround to sustain high-cadence deployment schedules.

The payload is heading to low Earth orbit, the ideal altitude for minimizing signal latency for the network. Operating in this region allows the satellites to deliver high-speed broadband services globally.

The launch will take place from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. This highly active pad serves as a primary eastern coast hub for rapid-turnaround commercial missions.
Watch for the precise ascent of the Falcon 9 as it works to deliver the Starlink payload into its designated deployment orbit. The mission is currently status Go for Launch.

This mission marks the second test flight of the Zhuque-3 vehicle under LandSpace's development program. It serves as a critical verification step to evaluate the overall system performance and collect flight data during this demonstration.

The flight utilizes the Zhuque-3 rocket, a next-generation launch vehicle developed by LandSpace. This mission will test the rocket's structural integrity and propulsion systems under active flight conditions.

The vehicle is targeting a low Earth orbit to deploy its test payload. Placing the spacecraft in this specific regime allows the team to evaluate its performance in a representative operational environment.

The launch will take place from Launch Area 96B at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in China. Operating from this established facility provides the necessary infrastructure and tracking assets for this developmental flight.

Observers should monitor the telemetry and propulsion performance of the Zhuque-3 during its ascent. A successful insertion into low Earth orbit will validate the vehicle's design and clear the path for future operational missions.

SpaceX is scheduled to launch the Starlink Group 17-49 mission to expand its global communications constellation. This dedicated flight continues the deployment of operational satellites to support high-speed internet delivery.
The mission utilizes the Falcon 9 Block 5, the workhorse of SpaceX's reusable fleet. This booster must execute a controlled landing following its ascent to allow for future refurbishment and flight.
The satellites are bound for low Earth orbit, which is ideal for minimizing signal latency for global communications. This orbit ensures high-speed data transmission for users worldwide.

The flight lifts off from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. This West Coast site provides a direct southerly trajectory to safely reach the required orbital inclination.
Watch for a precise orbital insertion of the payload and a rapid first-stage recovery attempt shortly after liftoff. This launch is officially marked as go for launch.

SpaceX is scheduled to launch the R-1 mission, representing a newly designated flight on their manifest. The August 15, 2026 departure marks the debut of this specific payload series under an unconfirmed status.
The mission utilizes the workhorse Falcon 9 Block 5, the flight-proven standard of the SpaceX fleet. This launch will rely on the booster's rapid turnaround capability to execute the R-1 deployment.
The payload is heading to low Earth orbit, the standard altitude band for high-speed deployment. This orbit keeps the R-1 satellite close to the planet to ensure rapid communication latency.

The rocket will lift off from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Flying from this West Coast location allows the Falcon 9 to safely clear the Pacific ocean during ascent.

This flight is worth watching to see the initial operational performance of the new R-1 payload series. Observers should monitor whether SpaceX can maintain the scheduled 2026 timeline as the target nears.
This SpaceX flight will deploy nine Globalstar 2-R communications satellites. This major cluster launch will significantly bolster the constellation's global mobile connectivity capabilities.
SpaceX is deploying its workhorse Falcon 9 Block 5 vehicle to lift these nine satellites. This flight will showcase the heavy-lift efficiency of this flight-proven booster system.
The satellites are destined for low Earth orbit to enable direct-to-device communication services. Operating at this altitude ensures minimal signal delay for the Globalstar network.
The mission will depart from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Flying from this active Florida pad provides excellent trajectory access to low Earth orbit.
Watch this flight to see how smoothly SpaceX deploys a large nine-satellite stack. Success will mark a major hardware refresh for Globalstar's orbital communication services.

China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation plans to launch an undisclosed payload aboard a Long March 12 rocket. Scheduled for August 17, 2026, the mission profile currently holds a status of To Be Confirmed.

This flight relies on the Long March 12 launch vehicle operated by China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation. The rocket is tasked with carrying the unannounced payload without published hardware modifications.
Target orbital parameters for this mission are listed as not available. Destination details remain unstated due to the non-public nature of the payload profile.
The launch is assigned to Commercial LC-2 at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in China. Conducting the flight from this pad supports the operational infrastructure for the Long March 12.

Monitoring updates from China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation will be essential given the To Be Confirmed status. Official verification of the August 17 schedule remains the primary operational milestone to watch.

SpaceX is deploying the Starlink Group 17-50 mission to expand its satellite communications network. Scheduled for August 19, 2026, at 02:00 UTC, this flight continues the dedicated deployment of orbital internet infrastructure.

The mission utilizes SpaceX's Falcon 9 Block 5 medium-lift launch vehicle. This configuration represents the final iterative upgrade of the Falcon 9 fleet designed for maximum reliability and reusability.
The payload is targeted for Low Earth Orbit to support global communication services. Operating in LEO provides the low latency required for real-time satellite internet connectivity.
Liftoff will occur from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg SFB in California. Flying from SLC-4E enables access to high-inclination orbital trajectories suited for this constellation group.
With an official status of Go for Launch, execution rests on precise timing at 02:00 UTC. Analysts will monitor stage separation and payload deployment into Low Earth Orbit.

China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation is targeting August 24, 2026, for the Chang'e 7 planetary science mission. This flight serves as a major step in exploration, though the launch status remains to be confirmed.

The Long March 5 rocket will transport this planetary science payload into space. Developed by China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation, it provides the heavy-lift capacity needed for deep-space tasks.
This mission targets Lunar Orbit, designated in flight data as LO. Operating from lunar orbit enables Chang'e 7 to perform its planetary science objectives.
Liftoff will occur from Launch Pad 101 at Wenchang Space Launch Site in China. The coastal facility supports the transportation and assembly of large Long March 5 rocket stages.

Because the mission status is To Be Confirmed, flight tracking should focus on timeline confirmation leading into August 2026. Successful insertion into lunar orbit will be the primary benchmark for this Long March 5 flight.
Arianespace is scheduled to launch the MTG-I2 mission on August 27, 2026, at 20:10 UTC. This Earth Science payload represents a key operational deployment for planetary monitoring.
The mission will be carried into space by the Ariane 62 launch vehicle. This configuration is tailored to deliver the MTG-I2 satellite on behalf of Arianespace.

The target destination for the MTG-I2 spacecraft is a Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO). Reaching GTO is the critical first stage in positioning the Earth Science satellite for its operational altitude.
Liftoff is set from Ariane Launch Area 4 at the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana. Operating from this French Guiana facility provides advantageous positioning for orbital insertion into GTO.

With a status of Go for Launch, the Ariane 62 is targeted for departure at 20:10 UTC on August 27, 2026. Monitors should focus on stage separation and clean injection into the intended GTO trajectory.
SpaceX is scheduled to launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on August 30, 2026. This dedicated astrophysics mission represents a significant deployment for space observatory research.
The mission relies on SpaceX's heavy-lift Falcon Heavy rocket. Its multi-core capability delivers the high performance necessary to accelerate the observatory payload.
The rocket will target the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2, commonly known as L2. Placing the telescope at L2 provides a stable environment for astrophysics observations.
Liftoff is set from Launch Complex 39A at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Executing from LC-39A provides the established infrastructure required for Falcon Heavy operations.
With a status of Go for Launch, countdown alignment remains on track for August 30, 2026. Flight analysts will monitor the upper-stage burn precision required to commit the payload toward L2.
